\section[esprimere]{esprimere — to express}

\label{lesson:IT-C345-esprimere}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for unquestionable, then the Italian for plain.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: esprimere}
\textbf{esprimere} — \textquotedblleft{}to express\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Non è facile esprimere quello che sento.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{It is not easy to express what I feel.}
\end{quote}

Past participle \emph{espresso} — the same word as the coffee, pressed out. \emph{Esprimersi} — to express yourself.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{esprimere} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{exprimere} \textquotedblleft{}to press out, to wring\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), built from \emph{ex-} \textquotedblleft{}out of\textquotedblright{} and \emph{premere} \textquotedblleft{}to press\textquotedblright{}: the thought is squeezed out into words.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esprimere}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{esprimere}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{esprimere}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for unquestionable, then the Italian for plain, then say \emph{esprimere} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does esprimere mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To express\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[affermare]{affermare — to state, to assert}

\label{lesson:IT-C345-affermare}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for plain, then the Italian for to express.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: affermare}
\textbf{affermare} — \textquotedblleft{}to state, to assert\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Il sindaco afferma che le tasse non aumenteranno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The mayor states that taxes will not rise.}
\end{quote}

Stronger than \emph{dire}. \emph{Affermarsi} is to become established, to succeed.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{affermare} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{affirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make firm, to assert\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built from \emph{ad} \textquotedblleft{}to\textquotedblright{} and \emph{firmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to strengthen\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{affermare}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{affermare}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{affermare}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for plain, then the Italian for to express, then say \emph{affermare} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does affermare mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To state, to assert\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[l'affermazione]{l'affermazione — the statement, the assertion}

\label{lesson:IT-C345-affermazione}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to express, then the Italian for to state.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: l'affermazione}
\textbf{l'affermazione} — \textquotedblleft{}the statement, the assertion\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
La tua affermazione non è vera.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Your statement is not true.}
\end{quote}

It also means success: \emph{l'affermazione di una squadra}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{affermazione} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{affirmātiō, affirmātiōnis} \textquotedblleft{}an assertion\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB), from \emph{affirmāre} \textquotedblleft{}to make firm\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{firmus} \textquotedblleft{}firm\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to express, then the Italian for to state, then say \emph{l'affermazione} again

\section[attendibile]{attendibile — credible, trustworthy (of news or a source)}

\label{lesson:IT-C345-attendibile}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for to state, then the Italian for the statement.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: attendibile}
\textbf{attendibile} — \textquotedblleft{}credible, trustworthy (of news or a source)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Questa notizia non è attendibile.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{This news is not reliable.}
\end{quote}

For information and sources: \emph{una notizia attendibile}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{attendibile} is built on \emph{attendere} in its old sense \textquotedblleft{}to pay heed to\textquotedblright{}, from Latin \emph{attendere} \textquotedblleft{}to stretch towards, to give heed\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{tendere} \textquotedblleft{}to stretch\textquotedblright{}: worth heeding.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{attendibile}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{attendibile}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for to state, then the Italian for the statement, then say \emph{attendibile} again

\section[affidabile]{affidabile — reliable, dependable}

\label{lesson:IT-C345-affidabile}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Italian for the statement, then the Italian for credible.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: affidabile}
\textbf{affidabile} — \textquotedblleft{}reliable, dependable\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Mio fratello è una persona affidabile: puoi lasciargli le chiavi.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My brother is a reliable person: you can leave him the keys.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Una macchina affidabile} — a reliable car.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{affidabile} is built on \emph{affidare} \textquotedblleft{}to entrust\textquotedblright{}, which comes from Vulgar Latin \emph{fīdāre}, a form of Latin \emph{fīdere} \textquotedblleft{}to trust\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short): someone you can trust things to.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{affidabile}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{affidabile}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{affidabile}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Italian for the statement, then the Italian for credible, then say \emph{affidabile} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does affidabile mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Reliable, dependable\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
